title: fix(web/UI): Address Book table columns + mobile view
description: ## What it solves Resolves: [WA-2715](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-2715/address-book-and-accounts-ui-feedback) Resolves: [WA-2649](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-2649/address-book-long-contact-names-not-truncated-text-overflows-into) Address Book & Accounts UI polish — cropped addresses, inconsistent chain tooltips, and non-scrollable tables on mobile. ## How this PR fixes it - **Full addresses**: widened the Address column on desktop across all Address Book tabs (Workspace / My contacts / Pending) so the full address is visible; bolded the first/last 4 bytes (`highlight4bytes`) in the Pending tab to match the other tabs. - **Chains column**: shows the first 3 chain logos + a `+N` badge (`showHasMore maxVisible={3}`) consistently on all tabs, and widened the column so 4+ chains no longer wrap. - **Requested by**: renders an address like the Address column (full, bold ends) or the name/email variant otherwise, with a hover tooltip (below the row) showing the full value. - **Accounts tooltip**: removed the "Multichain account on:" heading and reused the Address Book's chain-list layout so both show only the network names. - **Mobile**: gave all three tables a `min-w` so the existing `overflow-x-auto` container scrolls consistently (Workspace previously didn't), widened the Address column on small screens, and added spacing under the Pending tab. ## How to test it 1. Open a Workspace → Address Book on a wide desktop window — full addresses visible on Workspace / My contacts / Pending. 2. Add a contact spanning 4+ chains — Chains column shows 3 logos + `+N`, no wrapping. 3. Pending tab: "Requested by" shows a bold address (or name/email), full value on hover below the row. 4. Accounts list with a multichain Safe — tooltip lists network names only, no heading. 5. Narrow the viewport / open on mobile — all three tables scroll horizontally; extra margin under the Pending tab. ## Affected flows - Workspace Address Book: Workspace contacts, My contacts, and Pending requests tabs (view, chains display). - My Accounts list: multichain account chain badge tooltip. ## Blast radius - Feature-level changes only: `SpaceAddressBookTable`, `PendingRequestsTable`, `SpaceAddressBook/index`, `AccountItemChainBadge`. - Reuses shared `EthHashInfo`, `NetworkLogosList`, `ChainIndicator`, and `ui/tooltip`/`ui/table` — no shared primitives modified. - No API, feature-flag, persistence, or mobile-package changes. `NetworkLogosList` `+N` behavior was already supported via props. ## Risks / not checked - Did not verify with the private address book feature flag disabled (hides My contacts / Pending tabs). ## Visual summary **Before:** **After:** **Before:** **After:** - Full addresses - Tooltip on long names ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱 - [ ] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊 - [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻 - [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯 --- ## CLA signature With the submission of this Pull Request, I confirm that I have read and agree to the terms of the [Contributor License Agreement](https://safe.global/cla).

findings.claim: The test "exposes the full name via a tooltip trigger" only checks that the trigger button exists and never checks the tooltip content, so it does not assert the behaviour described by its own name.

The new test imports render from @testing-library/react instead of from @/tests/test-utils as required by the documented web testing convention (docs/engineering/conventions/web/project-structure.md, Testing section); most neighboring tests share this same violation, but AccountItemChainBadge.test.tsx in the same PR does it correctly.
The same isSmallScreen ternary condition is repeated across three header cell class names; using Tailwind breakpoint classes instead would remove the JS branching entirely.

This component detects small screens using MUI's useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('lg')), which switches at about 1200px, while the adjacent SpaceAddressBookTable.tsx uses the repo's useIsMobile() hook, which switches at 768px, so the two tabs on the same page change layout at different widths. The fix would be to use useIsMobile or plain Tailwind responsive classes, removing the MUI imports from this shadcn/Tailwind component.

The 'Requested by' column is fixed at w-[20%] (about 144-200px) while the full 42-character address with highlight4bytes needs roughly 300px, so combined with nowrap/ellipsis CSS the address is clipped from the right, hiding exactly the bold last-4-bytes highlight that the ellipsis cuts.

The full "Requested by" address is now rendered with shortAddress={false} inside a column about 144px wide at the new 720px minimum table width, and nothing truncates the text (only inline-flex min-w-0 is applied), so it will likely wrap or overflow; since the tooltip already shows the full value, the cell could instead use a short address or a truncate class.

The single-chain test asserts that a heading is absent, but that heading was never rendered in single-chain mode to begin with, so the assertion cannot actually fail and does not verify the intended behavior.

There are no tests covering the new small-screen column widths or the new showHasMore/maxVisible={3} props on NetworkLogosList, and the NetworkLogosList mock in this test file drops those props, so this new behaviour is untested.
react is imported twice in this file, once for useState and once for useMemo; these should be merged into a single import statement.
The tooltip trigger renders a <span> that wraps a <div>, which is invalid HTML nesting; using a <span> wrapper consistently or render={<div .../>} would fix it.

On small screens the table's column width percentages sum to 105% (15+40+15+20+15), and because the table uses table-fixed the browser rescales them, so the intended column proportions are never actually applied.
The email branch of the same cell renders an identicon for an email string instead of using EmailInfo, which is a rendering mismatch that a shared component like AddedBy already handles correctly.

TooltipTrigger renders a <button> by default, so every row gets a focusable button that performs no action, and the tooltip appears even for names that are not actually truncated; other places in the codebase instead pass render={<span .../>} to avoid this.

Removing the "Multichain account on:" heading changes the multichain tooltip everywhere this shared badge is used (it is exported through features/myAccounts/feature.ts, not only in the address book), which is a visible behaviour change outside the PR's stated address-book scope, and the PR description should reference the design decision behind it.

The pending-requests tests do not cover the showName behavior, the 'Requested by' tooltip, or the non-address strings returned by the API such as 'Unknown user' and 'Deleted user', leaving those code paths untested.

Column widths are switched in JavaScript via MUI's useMediaQuery(down('lg')) (1200px breakpoint), which returns false during server rendering, causing the widths to visibly jump after hydration; sibling tables instead use Tailwind responsive classes or a useIsMobile hook, which would avoid this jump.
The name-tooltip test only checks that a button element exists rather than verifying the tooltip's content, so it would not catch a regression in what the tooltip actually displays.

This PR adds a long-name tooltip to the address book Name column, but the Pending tab's own Name cell remains a bare truncate span without a tooltip; since that column also shrinks to 15% on small screens, long requester names get cut off with no way to read the full value.

The createSafeItem test fixture is hand-written with a hard-coded address and fixed values, even though the repo already provides safeItemBuilder() in apps/web/src/tests/builders/safeItem.ts that could be used instead, e.g. safeItemBuilder().with({ chainId }).build().

Tooltip* is mocked as a plain div in these tests, so the multichain test cannot verify that the content actually lives inside the tooltip; asserting that there is exactly one multichain-tooltip element would give a stronger check.

The wrapper
now appears twice in this file and again in SpaceAddressBookTable.tsx, and the two requestedBy branches differ only in a few props, so a small FullAddress helper or computing the props once would prevent the duplicated branches from drifting apart.

The single-chain test asserts that "Multichain account on:" is absent, but the single-chain branch never rendered that heading even before this change, so the assertion passes regardless of the change and cannot catch a regression.
The expression spaceId ?? '' is redundant at these locations because an earlier guard (if (!spaceId) return) already ensures spaceId is defined.

The address branch of the 'Requested by' cell now passes showName={false} to EthHashInfo, so admins always see the raw hex address instead of the requester's resolved name, even when that wallet is in the local or space address book, making it harder to identify who is asking for approval.
